verified_observations: ProjectMemory.open stores the project backlog at <project_root>/backlog.jsonl, while Manager _life_dir_for(mem) resolves the same project root and continuous state uses <life_dir>/continuous.json. Therefore the operator-priority backlog file and continuous.json share the same parent directory in this path.

Backlog._save calls _atomic_rewrite_jsonl. That helper writes a sibling temporary JSONL file, closes it, and os.replace()s it, but contains no explicit flush+os.fsync on the backlog file descriptor and no explicit directory fsync.

Continuous-state _atomic_write_bytes writes the continuous temp file, flushes it, os.fsyncs that file descriptor, invokes the before_replace callback, then os.replace()s continuous.json and finally fsyncs the parent directory.

manager_continuous_handoff passes its Manager/backlog commit as compare_and_swap_continuous_config(before_write=_commit); the callback can persist the operator-priority backlog item before continuous.json is replaced.

Linux fsync documentation distinguishes file-data durability from directory-entry durability: fsync(file) flushes file data/metadata, while a separate fsync(directory) is needed to ensure the containing directory entry reaches storage.

scope_refinement.worker_core_claim: Supported: backlog persistence does not have an explicit file-data fsync before a continuous objective can become durably enabled, so portable power-loss durability of the first mission row is not established by this code.
scope_refinement.refined_directory_claim: The worker's proposed requirement for a distinct backlog parent-directory fsync before the final continuous enable is stronger than necessary for this exact same-directory sequence. Because backlog.jsonl and continuous.json share the project directory, the continuous writer's final directory fsync occurs after both renames and can serve as the directory-metadata barrier for the earlier backlog rename. The remaining clear gap is the missing fsync of the backlog file contents before the continuous commit; a directory fsync is not a portable substitute for fsyncing that file's dirty data.
not_demonstrated: No power-loss or storage-fault experiment was executed.
No claim is made that data loss will occur on every filesystem or mount mode.
No performance claim is made about globally hardening every JSONL rewrite.
The proposed creation stamp, exact-insert API, handoff fence, route fingerprint v4, and durable backlog writer remain unimplemented adaptations.

test_observability.note: The public daemon portability tests exercise continuous replace/precommit failure behavior. No tracked test was found by direct repository search that asserts file-fsync ordering for _atomic_rewrite_jsonl.

decision_relevance: If the exact handoff invariant is implemented, the minimum durability primitive should explicitly fsync the authoritative backlog temp/file data before allowing the continuous commit. A separate earlier directory fsync is not independently required solely for same-directory rename metadata if the final continuous directory fsync is retained, though an implementation may still choose one for clearer transaction boundaries or other call sites.
exact_tested_scope: Static source-level audit at Argus commit 33da786bbc6787a2eeb63a5f492498eae87c78c7 plus filesystem synchronization semantics from Linux fsync documentation. No live crash injection or mutation.
